note: P57.1 candidate criteria in the exact P57 schema. This file is NOT imported by the application: it is validated by tests only. Each candidate needs Researcher review; to make one approvable it must be merged into data/scientific/p57-reference-criteria.v1.json through a reviewed patch (see IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md). Candidates without a catalog identity remain unapprovable. All are terrestrial general-population criteria; none is a NASA flight rule.

kinds.reference_interval: Range observed in a defined reference population (usually laboratory- and method-specific). Describes typical values, not disease.
kinds.diagnostic_threshold: Published cut point used, with stated confirmation requirements, as a criterion for a diagnosis. Meeting it is never itself a confirmed diagnosis.
kinds.risk_category: Published category boundaries used to stratify risk in a defined population. Not a diagnosis and not a reference interval.
kinds.action_threshold: Published value above or below which the source recommends a specific follow-up action (for example repeat testing).
kinds.critical_limit: Laboratory critical (panic) value requiring immediate clinician notification. None is seeded: no verified source was retrieved.
kinds.longitudinal_review_rule: Rule about change between examinations used for review triage. The existing P56.1 rules live in data/scientific/p56-review-priority-rules.v1.json and are not duplicated here; they never set RED, AMBER or NORMAL.
kinds.mission_operational_limit: Astronaut mission-specific operational limit. None is seeded: no verified astronaut-specific numerical criterion was retrieved.

criteria.title: Hyperkalaemia severity classification (UKKA 2026, adopting the ERC definition)
criteria.specimen: Serum or lithium-heparin plasma (specimen type must be recorded)
criteria.method: Laboratory analyser or point-of-care blood gas analyser

bands.label: Mild hyperkalaemia (UKKA)
bands.meaning: Serum potassium 5.5–5.9 mmol/L is classified by the UKKA guideline as mild hyperkalaemia; pseudohyperkalaemia must be excluded.

bands.label: Moderate hyperkalaemia (UKKA)
bands.meaning: Serum potassium 6.0–6.4 mmol/L is classified by the UKKA guideline as moderate hyperkalaemia.

bands.label: Severe hyperkalaemia (UKKA)
bands.meaning: Serum potassium of 6.5 mmol/L or higher is classified by the UKKA guideline as severe hyperkalaemia.

criteria.uncoveredMeaning: Values below 5.5 mmol/L are not categorized by this criterion, so no NORMAL status is derived from it; low potassium (hypokalaemia) is not covered. Values between published bounds (for example 5.95) are not classified.
criteria.highValues: Higher potassium in the stated ranges meets the guideline's hyperkalaemia severity classes, subject to exclusion of pseudohyperkalaemia and clinical confirmation.
criteria.lowValues: This criterion makes no statement about low potassium.
limitations: The source states there is no universally accepted definition of hyperkalaemia.
Pseudohyperkalaemia (haemolysis, long transit, delayed separation) must be excluded; unexpected results should be repeated.
Colour mapping (mild = AMBER, moderate and severe = RED) is a proposal of this package and needs Researcher approval.
RCUK/ERC 2025 text writes the severe class as '> 6.5' whereas UKKA writes '≥ 6.5'.
criteria.confirmation: Repeat measurement with paired lithium-heparin and clotted samples from a large vein with prompt analysis when pseudohyperkalaemia is suspected; clinical assessment by Ground Medical.

criteria.title: Hyponatraemia biochemical severity (ESE/ESICM/ERA-EDTA 2014)

bands.label: Mild hyponatraemia (biochemical, ESE)
bands.meaning: Serum sodium 130 to below 135 mmol/L is classified by the guideline as mild hyponatraemia (biochemical finding).

bands.label: Moderate hyponatraemia (biochemical, ESE)
bands.meaning: Serum sodium 125–129 mmol/L is classified by the guideline as moderate hyponatraemia (biochemical finding).

bands.label: Profound hyponatraemia (biochemical, ESE)
bands.meaning: Serum sodium below 125 mmol/L is classified by the guideline as profound hyponatraemia (biochemical finding).

criteria.uncoveredMeaning: Values of 135 mmol/L or higher are not categorized by this criterion, so no NORMAL status is derived from it; high sodium (hypernatraemia) is not covered. Values between published bounds (for example 129.5) are not classified.
criteria.highValues: This criterion makes no statement about high sodium.
criteria.lowValues: Lower sodium in the stated ranges meets the guideline's biochemical severity classes; symptom severity and acute versus chronic onset are classified separately by the source.
limitations: The source writes mild as 'between 130 and 135'; this candidate encodes the upper bound as below 135 because hyponatraemia is defined below 135 mmol/L. Researcher must confirm.
Hyperglycaemia must be excluded or sodium corrected for glucose before interpretation (source section 6.2.1.1).
Wording read from a full-text mirror; re-verify against the publisher PDF before approval.
criteria.confirmation: Confirm with repeat measurement by ion-specific electrode, exclude hyperglycaemia and assess symptoms and onset clinically (Ground Medical).

missionLevel.text: The crew members of this mission are adults.

perObservation.text: The observation records that sodium was measured by ion-specific electrode.
Hyperglycaemia is recorded as excluded for this sample (or a glucose-corrected sodium is recorded).

source.quote: We define 'mild' hyponatraemia as a biochemical finding of a serum sodium concentration between 130 and 135 mmol/l

criteria.title: Systolic value in hypertension stage ranges (2025 AHA/ACC guideline, per press release)

bands.label: Systolic in stage 1 hypertension range (AHA/ACC 2025)
bands.meaning: Systolic 130–139 mmHg is in the stage 1 hypertension range; the overall stage also depends on diastolic pressure.

bands.label: Systolic in stage 2 hypertension range (AHA/ACC 2025)
bands.meaning: Systolic of 140 mmHg or higher is in the stage 2 hypertension range.

criteria.uncoveredMeaning: Systolic values below 130 mmHg are not categorized per component: 'normal' and 'elevated' require both systolic and diastolic values, so no NORMAL status is derived. Low blood pressure is not covered.
criteria.highValues: Systolic values in the stated ranges fall in the guideline's hypertension stages when based on properly averaged readings.
criteria.lowValues: This criterion makes no statement about low blood pressure.
limitations: Source retrieved is the ACC press release; guideline full text and measurement protocol were not retrieved.
A single reading never establishes hypertension.
Per-component evaluation reports the component's stage range only; the overall category is the higher of both components.
criteria.confirmation: Confirm with averaged readings on separate occasions using a validated device, as specified by the guideline; Ground Medical decides follow-up.

missionLevel.text: The crew members of this mission are adults.

perObservation.text: The observation records that the value is an average of properly measured readings on more than one occasion.

criteria.title: Serum 25(OH)D status categories (NIH Office of Dietary Supplements)
criteria.method: 25(OH)D assay (method must be recorded; assays vary considerably)

bands.label: Associated with deficiency (NIH ODS)
bands.meaning: Below 12 ng/mL is associated with vitamin D deficiency (NIH ODS Table 1).

bands.label: Generally considered inadequate (NIH ODS)
bands.meaning: 12 to below 20 ng/mL is generally considered inadequate for bone and overall health in healthy individuals.

bands.label: Generally considered adequate (NIH ODS)
bands.meaning: 20–50 ng/mL is generally considered adequate for bone and overall health in healthy individuals.

bands.label: Linked to potential adverse effects (NIH ODS)
bands.meaning: Above 50 ng/mL is linked to potential adverse effects, particularly above 60 ng/mL.

criteria.uncoveredMeaning: All numeric values fall in one of the four categories.
criteria.highValues: Values above 50 ng/mL are linked by the source to potential adverse effects.
criteria.lowValues: Values below 20 ng/mL are generally considered inadequate; below 12 ng/mL are associated with deficiency.
limitations: The source states that 25(OH)D concentrations associated with deficiency have not been definitively identified.
The Endocrine Society (2024) states that outcome-specific thresholds have not been established and suggests against routine testing.
criteria.confirmation: Interpret with calcium, PTH, phosphate and bone-turnover context; Ground Medical decides any action.

perObservation.text: The observation records the 25(OH)D assay method.

source.quote: Associated with vitamin D deficiency, which can lead to rickets in infants and children and osteomalacia in adults

criteria.evidenceQuality: Government fact sheet summarizing Institute of Medicine-based categories; not a graded guideline.
